newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weak on lower interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weak on lower interest rates.

text.p: * Central Bank adjusts rates, triggers dollar-buying

The Philippine peso closed lower at 26.296 to the dollar from yesterday's 26.287 as some foreign investors shifted out of peso instruments following the slide in domestic interest rates, traders said.
"Some offshore investors are already closing their books this early, given that current level of interest rates are very low," one trader said.

Domestic long-termed interest rates fell this week due to excess liquidity in the system. Banks were locking in their funds in long-term issues fearing that interest rates would fall further when more funds are freed next year following the reduction in reserve requirements.

Another bank was also on the dollar buying mode to cover its huge commercial requirement. "This prompted the Central Bank to adjust its selling rate to 26.297 from 26.292 earlier in the day," another trader said.
The rate adjustment prompted other banks to buy dollars before the rate falls further.
Before the rate adjustment, banks were cautiously trading just above the 26.292 level.
The Central Bank sold about $35 million out of the $156.80 million traded in the market.
